data.title: Compose a museum room around a narrative
data.summary: Six owned objects, three story chapters and one existing room runtime. An LLM-assisted recipe with a concrete practice case, visual procedure and review gates.

facts.text: Cameras define the view and projection used to frame a scene.

prerequisites: An authorized Blender / Three.js environment and a recorded tool version. Blender-specific references here are pinned to the 4.5 manual; check differences in your installed version.
Practice inputs: Six owned objects, three story chapters and one existing room runtime.

Permission to use the source assets and a writable derived-output location. Use a disposable project copy for edits. An MCP connection is optional; reviewed scripts or manual tool actions can follow the same procedure.
steps: Inspect the existing project, asset registry and target runtime for an equivalent museum story room workflow. Reuse the closest source and preserve its original files.

Give Claude Code, Codex or another authorized coding assistant this practice brief: Six owned objects, three story chapters and one existing room runtime. Ask for a small plan and parameter/script diff; verify names and APIs against the installed tool version before applying it.
Reuse the room entrance and available display supports before adding new props
Place objects by story chapter with measured sightlines and label positions
Review the route from entrance to exit and keep a simple text alternative to each exhibit

Save the derived candidate separately, record software versions and source/output identities, then perform the acceptance checks. Keep unresolved quality, performance and rights questions in the receipt.
data.output: A versioned compose a museum room around a narrative candidate, the input/parameter table, source identity and a review receipt with the checks below.
validation: Every object has a readable label and provenance link
The route does not require camera teleportation to understand chapter order
Record actual observations separately from expected results; missing tests remain unrun.
limitations: A static gallery asset does not preserve the original runtime's interactions.
Sintra-authored proposal, not an executed Blender/engine/solver test. The diagram illustrates the procedure and is not a render or execution receipt.
Cloud chat cannot directly control a local 3D app without an appropriate authorized bridge. Tool access, model availability, paid services and rendering resources must be checked separately.
tips: Use the existing KONA/Studio room conventions when adapting private projects.
Let the LLM draft and explain bounded changes; use deterministic software to measure geometry, calculate trajectories and validate files.

data.prompt: Help me compose a museum room around a narrative in [existing authorized project]. First find an equivalent asset/workflow and inspect the installed tool version. Practice brief: Six owned objects, three story chapters and one existing room runtime. Propose the smallest parameter or script diff and explain each tool action. Follow the linked procedure, preserve original assets and stop on missing inputs or unsupported APIs. Check: Every object has a readable label and provenance link; The route does not require camera teleportation to understand chapter order. Return actual observations, source/output identities and blockers. Do not call expected results completed tests or publish private source paths.
